title: Bureau of Indian Standards — Core Institutional and Legal Framework
version: Current official BIS source; refresh regularly
content: BIS is India's national standards body. BIS operates under the BIS Act, 2016 and associated rules and regulations. The official BIS legal page provides the BIS Act 2016, BIS Rules 2018, BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018, BIS Hallmarking Regulations 2018 and related amendments/notifications. Questions about legal authority, certification, hallmarking, conformity assessment, enforcement or penalties should be grounded in the current Act, Rules, Regulations and notifications rather than generic assumptions.

title: Indian Standards — Meaning and lifecycle
content: An Indian Standard is a standard developed/adopted and published by BIS. Standards may cover products, processes, services, methods of test, terminology and other subjects. A standard can be revised, amended, reaffirmed, superseded or withdrawn. The current status and applicable amendments must be checked before giving a compliance answer. BIS's Know Your Standard portal is the official one-stop source for a selected standard and can expose the Indian Standard, amendments, gazette notifications, schemes of testing and inspection, licences, laboratories, classification and committee information.

title: BIS certification — voluntary and compulsory framework
content: BIS certification is basically voluntary. For specified products, the Central Government can make compliance compulsory through legal notifications and Quality Control Orders (QCOs). For a product under compulsory certification, the applicable order determines the relevant Indian Standard, conformity assessment route, Standard Mark/licence or Certificate of Conformity/registration requirements, scope, effective date and exemptions. Never infer that every Indian Standard requires a BIS licence; check the current QCO and BIS compulsory-certification list.

title: BIS Scheme-I Mark Scheme / Product Certification
version: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 as amended
content: Scheme-I is the principal BIS product certification mark scheme for use of the Standard Mark/ISI Mark on products covered by the applicable Indian Standard and certification scope. The manufacturer must have appropriate manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities. BIS assesses manufacturing capability and establishes product conformity through factory testing, third-party laboratory testing, or a combination as applicable. The official process includes application, assessment/inspection, sample testing, grant decision, marking conditions, surveillance, renewal, handling of non-conformity and possible suspension/cancellation. Requirements vary by product and current product manual/scheme of testing and inspection.

title: Compulsory Registration Scheme
content: Scheme-II is the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for notified products. Registration is based on conformity to the applicable Indian Standard and the requirements of the relevant order/scheme. The current BIS CRS pages and notifications must be checked for the product category, applicable standard, model/family scope, testing laboratory, registration process, marking and surveillance requirements. Do not assume CRS applies to a product merely because it is electronic; verify the current notified product list.

title: Certificate of Conformity (CoC)
version: BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations 2018 as amended
content: Scheme-IV provides a product certification route for grant of a Certificate of Conformity (CoC) under the BIS conformity assessment framework for applicable products/requirements. The exact product scope, conformity criteria, testing, assessment, surveillance and certificate conditions are governed by the applicable Indian Standard, notification and BIS guidelines. Use the current BIS scheme documents rather than a generic certification checklist.

title: BIS Scheme-X Certification
content: Scheme-X is a BIS certification/conformity assessment route applicable to products and categories notified under the relevant legal framework. The exact list of products, standards, testing, inspection, certificate/licence conditions and marking requirements must be checked from current BIS notifications and Scheme-X documents.

title: Quality Control Orders (QCOs) and mandatory certification
content: A Quality Control Order is a government notification that can make conformity to a specified Indian Standard compulsory for specified goods. A QCO may identify the product, Indian Standard, conformity assessment scheme, Standard Mark/licence or certificate/registration requirement, effective date, exemptions and other conditions. QCOs and amendments can change over time, so a compliance answer must use the latest notified order and BIS list.

title: Product Certification — Application to licence and surveillance
content: For applicable Scheme-I product certification, BIS provides guidelines covering grant of licence, additional guidelines, product non-conformity, unsatisfactory performance, scope changes, renewal, sample retesting, factory surveillance, market surveillance and cluster-based test facilities for MSMEs. Application is accepted online through the BIS/e-BIS system. A manufacturer needs suitable infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capability and the product must meet all relevant requirements of the Indian Standard. The exact steps and fees depend on the product and applicable scheme.

title: BIS licence, eligibility, application, fees, renewal and enforcement FAQ
content: BIS defines a licence as permission under Section 13 of the BIS Act 2016 to use a specified Standard Mark for goods/articles conforming to a standard. Manufacturers need manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities. BIS may establish conformity through factory assessment and laboratory testing. Application is online. Fees, timelines, validity, renewal, suspension/cancellation and conditions are governed by current regulations and product-specific documents; do not generalize product-specific fees or timelines.

title: FMCS — certification for foreign manufacturers
content: BIS's Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) provides a route for eligible foreign manufacturers to obtain BIS certification/licensing for applicable products. Requirements include product conformity, manufacturing/testing capability, inspection/assessment and compliance with the applicable Indian Standard and scheme requirements. The current BIS FMCS guidance and product-specific documents control eligibility, marking, authorised Indian representative requirements, fees, surveillance and renewal.

title: BIS Hallmarking — meaning, purpose and scope
content: Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in precious-metal articles. Hallmarks are official marks used as a guarantee of purity or fineness. BIS states that gold and silver are presently under the Hallmarking Scheme in India. The scheme protects consumers against adulteration and supports legal standards of fineness. The current BIS hallmarking pages contain regulations, mandatory hallmarking orders, jeweller registration, A&H centre requirements, refinery requirements, consumer testing and related forms.

title: Hallmarking Regulations — jewellers, A&H centres and refineries
content: The BIS Hallmarking Regulations, 2018 include provisions covering registration of jewellers, recognition of Assaying and Hallmarking Centres and licensing of refineries/mints. The regulations have been amended. Compliance answers must use the current consolidated legal requirements and latest amendments published by BIS.

title: Mandatory hallmarking — orders, QCOs, amendments and district coverage
content: BIS maintains the Mandatory Hallmarking Order page with the original order, amendments, Quality Control Orders, exemptions/guidelines and phase-wise district coverage. Mandatory coverage is legally time-sensitive and can change by notification. Always check the latest order and amendment for the article type, metal, purity, location/district, effective date and exemptions.

title: Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking
content: BIS hallmarking FAQ lists IS 1417:2016 for Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking — Specification. Questions about gold jewellery purity/fineness and hallmarking should be checked against the current BIS standard, amendments and mandatory hallmarking order.

title: Silver and Silver Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking
version: Check current BIS status and amendments
content: BIS hallmarking FAQ lists the Indian Standard for silver and silver-alloy jewellery/artefacts covering fineness and marking. Because silver hallmarking requirements have changed, verify the current standard, amendments and mandatory/voluntary provisions on the latest BIS hallmarking pages before giving a compliance decision.

title: Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID)
content: HUID is the Hallmark Unique Identification number used for traceability of hallmarked articles. BIS provides consumer verification guidance through the BIS CARE App and its hallmarking FAQ. The exact marking requirements and applicability must be checked against the latest BIS notifications and applicable metal/article standard.

title: BIS registration for jewellers selling hallmarked articles
content: BIS states that a jeweller willing to sell hallmarked gold and silver jewellery/artefacts applies online for BIS registration. The current BIS page states that the certificate of registration is granted without a registration fee and is valid for lifetime, subject to the applicable legal conditions. It also explains who is required to register, point-of-sale responsibility and the process for sending jewellery to a recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre. Verify current turnover exemptions and mandatory coverage because government notifications can change.

title: Assaying and Hallmarking Centres — recognition and operation
content: IS 15820 provides requirements for establishment and operation of Assaying and Hallmarking Centres. BIS recognition involves infrastructure, quality management, trained/competent personnel and assessment. A registered jeweller submits articles to a recognized A&H centre, where testing/assaying is performed and articles meeting requirements are hallmarked. The current BIS A&H guidelines govern grant, operation, renewal, suspension and cancellation.

title: BIS licensing of refineries and mints
content: BIS provides a scheme for hallmarking bullion/coins by refineries/mints. The current BIS page states the present scope is gold and describes prerequisites such as in-house manufacturing/testing capability and laboratory accreditation by NABL or LBMA, subject to the applicable requirements. Scope, fineness, design/weight, fees and licence validity are controlled by current BIS documents.

title: Consumer verification/testing of hallmarked jewellery
content: Consumers can have hallmarked or unhallmarked precious-metal articles tested at BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centres on a chargeable basis. BIS provides consumer guidance on invoices, purity/fineness, hallmark information, HUID verification and complaint/redressal. Use the current BIS FAQ for exact testing charges and procedures because fees and rules can change.

title: BIS recognized laboratories and testing infrastructure
content: BIS maintains laboratory and testing services and publishes information about recognized/testing laboratories and capabilities. For a certification question, the applicable product manual or scheme may specify acceptable testing arrangements. Do not claim that a particular lab can test a product unless its current BIS scope confirms that capability.

title: BIS consumer protection, complaints and misuse of Standard Mark
content: BIS provides consumer-oriented services including complaint handling, awareness, product recalls/alerts and mechanisms for reporting misuse of BIS Standard Marks or non-conforming products. Consumers should retain invoices and relevant product/marking evidence. Current BIS consumer guidance controls the complaint channel and procedure.

title: How Indian Standards are formulated, revised and maintained
content: BIS develops and maintains Indian Standards through technical committees and stakeholder participation. Standards may be new, revised, reaffirmed, amended or withdrawn. Draft standards can be circulated for comments. The current status and amendments of a specific standard should be verified through Know Your Standard and related BIS publications.

title: Official BIS standard intelligence portal
content: The Know Your Standard feature is BIS's one-stop access point for documents and data related to a selected standard. A standard can be searched by IS number or keyword/product name. BIS states that the portal can expose the Indian Standard, amendments, gazette notifications, scheme of testing and inspection, licences, laboratories, classification details and committee information. The application should link users to this official source whenever a requested standard is not available in the local evidence store.

title: Applications and official forms
content: BIS publishes official forms and formats for services including jeweller registration, Assaying and Hallmarking Centre recognition, refinery/mint licensing and renewals. Use the current BIS form rather than copying an old form or assuming a fixed fee.

title: BIS management system certification services
content: BIS provides management systems certification services in applicable areas. The exact scheme, standard, eligibility, audit, certification, surveillance and renewal requirements are specific to the management system and current BIS scheme. Examples may include quality, environmental, occupational health and safety and other systems where BIS offers certification. Verify current BIS scope before giving a specific requirement.

title: BIS Eco Mark scheme
content: BIS provides information on the Eco Mark scheme and applicable environmental/product criteria. The current scheme documents and notifications determine eligibility, assessment and marking. Do not assume Eco Mark is equivalent to ordinary BIS product certification.

title: BIS standards in emerging technology and industry areas
content: BIS develops standards in emerging areas, including newer technology and industrial sectors. The current BIS emerging-areas pages and Know Your Standard portal should be used to discover applicable standards rather than relying on a fixed static list.
